description: Supersede ADR-0049: product name moves from GARBOARD (fatal live-homonym collision at garboard.dev) to GATESHIP, formalize the four-layer name gate, and sweep the artifacts that present the old name

userStories.title: Write ADR-0050 (GATESHIP supersedes GARBOARD) and append the supersession note to ADR-0049
userStories.description: As the operator, I need an explicit supersession ADR that registers GATESHIP as the product name, records the measured reason GARBOARD died, formalizes the four-layer name gate that was missing, and preserves ADR-0049 untouched except for an appended supersession pointer, so that the naming decision is closed on the record and never re-litigated from zero.
acceptanceCriteria: A new ADR exists at docs/adr/0050-gateship-supersedes-garboard-naming.md registering GATESHIP as the product name and explicitly naming ADR-0049 as the superseded record (AC1, new-side pointer). [oracle: grep -qi 'gateship' docs/adr/0050-gateship-supersedes-garboard-naming.md && grep -q '0049' docs/adr/0050-gateship-supersedes-garboard-naming.md]

ADR-0049 carries a supersession note pointing to ADR-0050 (AC1, old-side pointer), added as an append at the end of the file. [oracle: grep -q '0050' docs/adr/0049-garboard-naming-policy-binary-alias-org-and-staged-rename.md]

ADR-0049 is append-only relative to main: the main version is an exact prefix of the branch version (invariance pin, deliberately green on main; USE THIS EXACT FORM, do not invent another). [oracle: diff <(git show main:docs/adr/0049-garboard-naming-policy-binary-alias-org-and-staged-rename.md) <(head -n "$(git show main:docs/adr/0049-garboard-naming-policy-binary-alias-org-and-staged-rename.md | wc -l)" docs/adr/0049-garboard-naming-policy-binary-alias-org-and-staged-rename.md)]

ADR-0050 records the measured motive of the change (AC2): garboard.dev is a LIVE adjacent product (a web-app builder that verifies generated apps against machine-checkable criteria before shipping, i.e. the same thesis we sell), garboard.app is taken on the same Vercel nameservers (same probable owner), and garboard.com is parked for sale on afternic; the record says WHY the name died, not merely that it changed. [oracle: grep -qi 'garboard\.dev' docs/adr/0050-gateship-supersedes-garboard-naming.md && grep -qi 'garboard\.app' docs/adr/0050-gateship-supersedes-garboard-naming.md && grep -qi 'garboard\.com' docs/adr/0050-gateship-supersedes-garboard-naming.md]

ADR-0050 formalizes the four-layer name gate as a checklist to run BEFORE adopting any future name: (1) domain, (2) npm, (3) GitHub org, (4) live homonymous product in the category and adjacent categories (AC3); layers 1-3 tokens are greppable. [oracle: grep -qi 'npm' docs/adr/0050-gateship-supersedes-garboard-naming.md && grep -qi 'github' docs/adr/0050-gateship-supersedes-garboard-naming.md]
The fourth layer is explicit as ELIMINATORY, in the AC3 wording: domain availability is not the test, occupation of the term by an adjacent live product is. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

ADR-0050 records the evidence sustaining GATESHIP (AC4): no commercial owner of the term on any surveyed surface; .dev/.io/.app/.ai unregistered; npm, PyPI and crates without a package; the only occupations being the GitHub org gateship-one (Android Odyssey player, 255 stars, no commercial pretension) and Stargate fandom corpus; plus the accepted cost that gateship.com has been registered since 2005 and dormant without nameservers, so the .com is not ours today. [oracle: grep -qi 'gateship-one' docs/adr/0050-gateship-supersedes-garboard-naming.md && grep -qi 'gateship\.com' docs/adr/0050-gateship-supersedes-garboard-naming.md && grep -qi 'stargate' docs/adr/0050-gateship-supersedes-garboard-naming.md]

ADR-0050 records every eliminated candidate with its eliminatory reason (AC5): keelgate, deckrun, shipset, gatework, bowmark, keelward, wayhelm, gatepath, gaterun, the whole helm- prefix, and the runners-up prowmark (one letter from Promark) and deckward (Deckard homophone). [oracle: grep -qi 'keelgate' docs/adr/0050-gateship-supersedes-garboard-naming.md && grep -qi 'deckrun' docs/adr/0050-gateship-supersedes-garboard-naming.md && grep -qi 'shipset' docs/adr/0050-gateship-supersedes-garboard-naming.md && grep -qi 'gatework' docs/adr/0050-gateship-supersedes-garboard-naming.md && grep -qi 'bowmark' docs/adr/0050-gateship-supersedes-garboard-naming.md && grep -qi 'keelward' docs/adr/0050-gateship-supersedes-garboard-naming.md && grep -qi 'wayhelm' docs/adr/0050-gateship-supersedes-garboard-naming.md && grep -qi 'gatepath' docs/adr/0050-gateship-supersedes-garboard-naming.md && grep -qi 'gaterun' docs/adr/0050-gateship-supersedes-garboard-naming.md && grep -qi 'helm' docs/adr/0050-gateship-supersedes-garboard-naming.md && grep -qi 'prowmark' docs/adr/0050-gateship-supersedes-garboard-naming.md && grep -qi 'deckward' docs/adr/0050-gateship-supersedes-garboard-naming.md]

userStories.notes: Files: docs/adr/0050-gateship-supersedes-garboard-naming.md (new), docs/adr/0049-garboard-naming-policy-binary-alias-org-and-staged-rename.md (EOF append only). Write ADR-0050 in English mirroring ADR-0049's structure (Context/Decision/Consequences), since it supersedes that record. SUPERSESSION DOCTRINE (issue gotcha): ADR-0049 must NEVER be edited in place; the historical record of the error is part of the value. The only change to 0049 is a supersession block APPENDED after its last line ('Superseded by ADR-0050: <reason one-liner>'); do not touch the title, Context, Decision or Consequences text. The append-only pin oracle is DELIBERATELY GREEN ON MAIN (invariance pin, not red-on-main); its falsifiability sweep was already executed by the orchestrator on 2026-07-27 in a throwaway worktree with 4 reproducible results: main untouched exit 0; deleting a mid-file markdown bullet exit 1; rewriting an existing line exit 1; appending a supersession block at EOF exit 0. ORACLE LINT RULE (applies to any oracle you add in tests too): never compare against an integer literal (-eq/-ne/etc.) without a live re-derivation token (git show main:, git diff main, git grep ... main) in the SAME clause; for invariance prefer integer-free forms (prefix identity, content equality, empty set). SCOPE OF THE DECISION: ADR-0050 registers the product name GATESHIP and the name gate; carry forward 0049's staged-rename doctrine (display layer moves now, binary rename at launch packaging, internal contracts CAM_*/cam never rename) with GATESHIP replacing GARBOARD as the target, and explicitly reaffirm ADR-0045's display-only doctrine. Do NOT invent policy the operator did not decide: 0049's typed alias 'gar' was garboard-derived, so record the alias as re-decided at launch packaging rather than coining a new one. Order by merit presented to the operator was gateship > prowmark > deckward; decision GATESHIP on 2026-07-27 after a 21-candidate four-layer triage. Do not rename the binary, code identifiers, or buy domains (out of scope per issue). ADR admission gates (hard to reverse / surprising / genuine trade-off) all pass; say so briefly as 0049 did.

userStories.notes: Files: docs/positioning.md (22 garboard occurrences, mostly section '4. Naming decision' with subsections 4.1-4.6), docs/launch-readiness.md (3 occurrences around line 74: 'canonical binary moves from cam to garboard'). Depends on US-001: cite ADR-0050 by its real filename. positioning.md section 4 should present GATESHIP as the settled name citing ADR-0050 and keep only what a reader needs (the ADRs own the full 5-round history and kill evidence); watch for the CAM-415 review lesson recorded in the journal: the file self-contradicted once by describing the product under one name in sections 1-3 while section 4.5 demoted that name, so re-read the WHOLE file for name coherence after the edit. Alias policy (4.5) and reserves (4.6): reconcile with what ADR-0050 actually decides (alias re-decided at launch packaging; do not invent a new alias). HARD CONSTRAINT (ADR-0036 / CAM-162 defect class): do NOT edit anything under scripts/cam/issues/, scripts/cam/journal.md, scripts/cam/suggestions.jsonl or CHANGELOG.md on this branch; the three git-show-main oracles are satisfied by the orchestrator/operator editing those issue records directly on main during this cycle, and the reviewer's Layer B gate re-runs them independently. If they are still red at your verification step, report the story DONE-blocked-on-main via worker-report rather than editing control-plane files. The AC6 grep oracle's exclusion list is the planner's encoding of the AC's own exemption rationale ('onde o nome antigo e o assunto do registro') extended to append-only history and worker-denied control-plane records; the on-main oracles above close the gap for the open records that DID present garboard as current. Doc-as-code gate (ADR-0037) detects path claims in markdown by heuristic: keep any file paths you touch in these docs real. Oracle-lint rule from the issue applies to all oracles: no integer-literal comparison without live re-derivation in the same clause (the test -z form used here is integer-free by design).
